forecaster_note: Plenty of leftover S swell mixing with shorter-period NE wind wave for peaky, fun to decent-sized surf — chest to head high at most breaks, occasional overhead sets at the S-facing spots. Light offshore early but still junky from the short-period swell; N corners and S-facing breaks hold the best form. NE winds pick up later morning. Fri: waist–chest, peaky, best around dawn. Sat: light NW'lies in the morning for a clean wave before NE'lies. Sun: onshore and lumpy, small clean wave in the sheltered corners. — Hugh McDowell, Surfline

wind.summary: NNE cross-shore 11kph (gust 25) at dawn — swings NE onshore 17kph by 9am, 19–24kph gusting 30 by the afternoon.

days.label: Today
days.note: Short-period NE windswell (6ft @ 7s, 57°) over a leftover S groundswell (2.2ft @ 11s). NNE cross early, NE onshore from ~9am — dawn to 9am is it. Long Reef and Curl Curl hold Fair at 3–5ft; Dee Why and Manly sit Poor-Fair.

dee-why.window: Dawn–9am while the wind is still NNE cross; high tide 6:38am, so the Point improves as it drains toward mid-morning — but the NE onshore arrives first.
alerts: NE onshore builds from ~9am — 17kph, then 19–24kph gusting 30 through the afternoon

tip.label: Frontside at the Point
tip.text: 57° NE windswell has enough E in it to reach the Point, but at 7s it's soft and wobbly. Pick the bigger sets on the drop tide, stay tight in the pocket on your rights — the 11s S pulse adds the odd punchier one.

long-reef.window: 6–9am — the pick today. Light offshore at dawn and 4–5ft peaks by 9am before the NE fills in.
alerts: NE onshore builds from ~9am — 17kph, then 19–24kph gusting 30 through the afternoon

tip.label: Pick your peak
tip.text: Most size on the strip. Short-period peaks mean lefts and rights — take the lefts backside with a strong bottom turn, and don't hang around once the NE hits.

curl-curl.window: Dawn session — 3–4ft Fair at 6am, drops to Poor-Fair by 9am as the NE onshore bites.
alerts: NE onshore builds from ~9am — 17kph, then 19–24kph gusting 30 through the afternoon

tip.label: South end first
tip.text: The S-end corner gets a touch of protection from the NE — start there and work the peaky banks early.

manly.window: Only worth it at dawn if you're local — onshore and small all day.
alerts: NE onshore builds from ~9am — 17kph, then 19–24kph gusting 30 through the afternoon

tip.label: Longboard it
tip.text: Thigh–stomach and onshore — a log or grovel board makes the most of it. Save the energy for Long Reef.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: NE windswell holds (~6ft @ 7s, 46°) with the S swell fading. Light NNE cross at dawn, NE onshore by midday — first light to 10am. Long Reef and Curl Curl Fair at 3–4ft.

dee-why.window: Dawn–10am with light NNE cross 9–10kph; onshore 17–24kph from midday.

long-reef.window: 6–10am — light offshore early, holds Fair into midday.

curl-curl.window: 6–10am — offshore at dawn, Fair until the NE fills in.

manly.window: Dawn only — onshore most of the day.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Saturday morning is the weekend pick: light NW offshore (6–8kph) and a clean 2–4ft NE windswell, Fair everywhere until NE'lies around midday. Sunday goes S-onshore and lumpy (Poor), though energy climbs late Sun (368kJ) with 4–5ft at Long Reef.

dee-why.window: Sat 6–10am — NW offshore, clean. Sun onshore and Poor.

long-reef.window: Sat 6–11am — clean 3–4ft on the NW. Sun building to 4–6ft late but S onshore.

curl-curl.window: Sat 6–10am — offshore, up to shoulder high. Sun onshore.

manly.window: Sat 6–11am clean and Fair. Sun Poor-Fair, 3–4ft cross-shore.
